n869f606043a.s: In how many of the eleven provinces did the Congress form ministries after the 1937 elections?
n869f606043a.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces, including Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, UP, NWFP and Assam.

ncdeb402f31e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events of 1939-40?
o: Linlithgow declared India a party to the Second World War in September 1939
The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939
The Muslim League observed Deliverance Day on 22 December 1939
The Lahore Resolution was adopted before the Congress ministries resigned
ncdeb402f31e.x: The Lahore Resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940, after the ministries resigned in October-November 1939; the other three are correct.

ncd9933fbf3b.s: How did the Muslim League fare in the 1937 provincial elections?
o: It did poorly even in Muslim seats
It won a clear majority in Bengal
It formed ministries in all Muslim-majority provinces
ncd9933fbf3b.x: The League performed poorly even in Muslim seats, after which it alleged 'Hindu Raj' and launched mass-contact campaigns.

nda29b02cda9.s: Whose contribution to the separate Muslim homeland idea came earliest, in 1887?
nda29b02cda9.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan came first (1887), followed by Iqbal (1930), Rahmat Ali (1933) and Jinnah (1940).

new.s: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 by the government of which British Prime Minister?
new.x: The Conservative government of Stanley Baldwin appointed it to study the working of the 1919 Act; MacDonald was PM during the Round Table Conferences.

new.s: How many members did the Simon Commission have?
new.x: It had seven members, all British, headed by Sir John Simon.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Simon Commission:
1. It was headed by Sir John Simon of the Liberal Party.
2. Clement Attlee was one of its members.
3. It had one Indian member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Simon (Liberal) headed it and Attlee was a member; it had no Indian member, which is why it was boycotted.

new.s: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on:
new.x: It arrived on 3 February 1928; 26 February 1928 was the Madras protest and 11 October 1928 began its second visit.

new.s: Lala Lajpat Rai died of injuries from a lathi charge while leading the anti-Simon protest at:
new.x: Lajpat Rai led the 1928 Lahore protest and died of the lathi-charge injuries.

new.s: The Simon Commission was boycotted mainly because:
o: It was headed by a Conservative
new.x: An all-British, seven-member commission with no Indian member was boycotted with the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.

new.s: Who was the President of the Andhra Boycott Committee against the Simon Commission?
new.x: S. Satyamurthy presided the Andhra Boycott Committee; Unnayya Sastri led Tenali-Guntur and Kaleswara Rao was Vijayawada's municipal chairman.

new.s: Which pair relating to the Simon boycott in Andhra is correctly matched?
o: Tenali and Guntur – Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
new.x: Kaleswara Rao, Vijayawada municipal chairman, issued a cover reading only 'Simon Go Back'; Unnayya Sastri led Tenali and Guntur.

new.s: The All Parties Conference that set up the Nehru Report committee was presided over by:
new.x: Ansari presided the All Parties Conference; Motilal Nehru chaired the drafting committee.

new.s: The Nehru Report demanded which status for India?
new.x: It sought dominion status; Jawaharlal Nehru and Bose wanted complete independence.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nehru Report:
1. It recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities.
2. It recommended a Supreme Court.
3. It was submitted at Lucknow in August 1928.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: joint electorates with reserved seats, a bicameral centre with a Supreme Court, and submission at Lucknow on 28 August 1928.

new.s: After the Nehru Report, the Congress ultimatum led to the Purna Swaraj resolution at which session?
new.x: The one-year ultimatum led to Purna Swaraj at Lahore in December 1929; Jinnah's amendments had failed at Calcutta in 1928.

new.s: The Delhi Proposals of March 1927 demanded the separation of which region from Bombay?
new.x: The Delhi Proposals asked for a separate Sindh, one-third central seats and reforms in NWFP and Baluchistan.

new.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points wanted residuary powers vested in the:
new.x: The Fourteen Points sought a federal constitution with residuary powers to the provinces.

new.s: The Butler Committee of 1927 was headed by:
new.x: Sir Harcourt Butler headed it, not Irwin; its 1929 report upheld paramountcy.

new.s: Besides declaring dominion status as India's goal, the Deepavali Declaration of 1929 promised:
o: A Round Table Conference after the Simon report
new.x: Irwin's declaration of 31 October 1929 promised a Round Table Conference after the Simon report.

new.s: The Simon Commission report recommended separating which territory from India?
new.x: It proposed separating Burma from India and Sindh from Bombay.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Simon Commission report?
o: It recommended abolishing dyarchy in the provinces
It recommended keeping separate communal electorates
It became the base of the Government of India Act, 1935
It recommended a separate Andhra province
new.x: The report created Orissa but ignored Andhra's demand; the other statements are correct.

new.s: How many delegates attended the Third Round Table Conference?
new.x: Only 46 delegates attended the Third RTC (Nov-Dec 1932), from which Congress and Jinnah were absent.

new.s: Which of the following leaders was absent from the Third Round Table Conference?
new.x: Jinnah was absent from the Third RTC; Ambedkar and Sapru attended all three.

new.s: The White Paper that led to the Government of India Act, 1935 followed which Round Table Conference?
new.x: The Third RTC (1932) produced the White Paper leading to the 1935 Act.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
2. Nehru Report
3. Rowlatt Act
4. Simon Commission appointed
new.x: Rowlatt Act (1919), Simon Commission (1927), Nehru Report (1928), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

new.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on:
new.x: It was signed on 5 March 1931, after which Gandhi agreed to attend the Second RTC.

new.s: Which Congress session of 1936 decided to contest the elections under the Government of India Act, 1935?
new.x: Faizpur (1936) decided to contest; Lucknow (1936) had rejected the Act.

new.s: The Congress rejected the Government of India Act, 1935 at its 1936 session held at:
new.x: The Lucknow session of 1936, presided over by Nehru, rejected the Act.

new.s: The provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935 were held in:
new.x: Elections were held in winter 1936-37 in 11 provinces; ministries followed in 1937.

new.s: Provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 came into force on:
new.x: Provincial autonomy began on 1 April 1937, with Governors keeping reserve powers.

new.s: Which of the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 was NOT implemented?
o: Abolition of the Council of India
new.x: The Federation never came into force because too few princes acceded; the others were implemented.

new.s: The Federal Court under the Government of India Act, 1935 was set up at Delhi in:
new.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in October 1937.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. Dyarchy at the Centre never came into force.
2. The Council of India advising the Secretary of State was abolished.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: central dyarchy was part of the unrealised federal scheme, and the Council of India was abolished.

new.s: How many subjects did the Provincial List contain under the Government of India Act, 1935?
new.x: The lists had 59 (Federal), 54 (Provincial) and 36 (Concurrent) subjects.

new.s: The Concurrent List under the Government of India Act, 1935 had how many subjects?
new.x: The Concurrent List had 36 subjects; Federal 59 and Provincial 54.

new.s: In 1934, the demand for a Constituent Assembly was first raised by M.N. Roy. In which year did the Congress adopt it officially?
new.x: M.N. Roy raised it in 1934 and the Congress adopted it officially in 1935.

new.s: After the 1937 elections, the Punjab ministry was formed by the Unionist Party under:
new.x: Sikandar Hayat Khan's Unionist Party formed the Punjab ministry; there was no Congress ministry there.

new.s: In Bengal after the 1937 elections, the coalition ministry was led by:
new.x: Congress lacked an absolute majority in Bengal; Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party led the coalition.

new.s: In the 1937 elections in Sindh, the coalition ministry was formed under:
new.x: Sindh had a coalition under Allah Baksh.

new.s: In the 1937 Madras Congress ministry, Bezawada Gopala Reddy held which portfolio?
new.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Local Self-Government; Prakasam was Revenue and V.V. Giri Labour and Industries.

new.s: Which Andhra leader was Minister for Labour and Industries in the 1937 Madras ministry?
new.x: V.V. Giri held Labour and Industries; Sambamurthy was Speaker.

new.s: Rajaji's introduction of Hindi in Madras schools in 1937 led to an agitation led by:
new.x: Periyar led the anti-Hindi agitation of 1937, and the measure was withdrawn.

new.s: In how many provinces did the Congress win a clear majority on its own in 1937?
new.x: It won a clear majority in five (Madras, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa) but formed ministries in eight.

new.s: Which labour law was passed during the Congress ministries of 1937-39?
new.x: The Congress ministries passed the Industrial Disputes Act (1938) and protected trade-union rights.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of the Congress ministries of 1937-39?
o: Introduction of separate electorates for labour
new.x: Separate electorates for labour came from the 1935 Act itself; the ministries released prisoners, passed tenancy laws and abolished begar.

new.s: Lord Linlithgow declared India at war with Germany, without consulting Indian leaders, on:
new.x: The declaration on 3 September 1939 led the Congress ministries to resign in Oct-Nov 1939.

new.s: Which of the following was borrowed into the Constitution from the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Public Service Commissions and the office of Governor
new.x: The 1935 Act gave the federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary, PSCs and emergency provisions.

new.s: The 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act, 1935 served as the model for:
new.x: The Instrument of Instructions was the model for the DPSP, not Fundamental Rights.

new.s: Separate electorates are seen as the seed of the Two-Nation Theory because they:
new.x: Separate electorates institutionalised religion in representation, sowing the seed of the Two-Nation Theory.

new.s: The Two-Nation Theory was formally set out in:
new.x: The Lahore Resolution of 1940 formally set out the Two-Nation Theory.

new.s: Who is called the 'Father of Communal Electorate'?
new.x: Lord Minto is called the Father of Communal Electorate, after the 1909 Morley-Minto Reforms.

new.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 extended separate electorates to:
o: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans
new.x: The 1919 Act extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; the 1932 Award and 1935 Act extended them further.

new.s: Separate electorates were extended to the depressed classes by the:
new.x: The Communal Award (1932) extended them to the depressed classes; the Poona Pact replaced it with reserved seats.

new.s: Lord Dufferin used Sayyid Ahmad Khan as an anti-Congress front together with:
new.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan was used with Raja Shiva Prasad of Benares and the Raja of Bhinga in 1887-88.

new.s: The United Indian Patriotic Association was formed in:
new.x: It was formed in 1888 as an anti-Congress front.

new.s: Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address proposed a consolidated Muslim state in which part of India?
new.x: Iqbal proposed a consolidated Muslim state in the North-West.

new.s: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakistan' as a student of:
new.x: He coined it in 1933 as a Cambridge student.

new.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Muslim League in March 1940?
new.x: Jinnah presided; Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted and Fazlul Huq moved the resolution.

new.s: In reply to the Lahore Resolution, Periyar demanded Dravidistan at which conference in 1940?
new.x: Periyar demanded Dravidistan at the Erode Conference, 1940.

new.s: The Lahore Resolution demanded:
o: Independent states for Muslims in Muslim-majority areas
A single federation with weak Centre
new.x: It demanded independent states for Muslims in Muslim-majority areas and was soon called the Pakistan Resolution.

new.s: Direct Action Day was observed by the Muslim League on:
new.x: Direct Action Day was 16 August 1946, called for Pakistan; it led to the Calcutta killings.

new.s: Who prepared the Pirpur Report of 1938?
o: Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur
new.x: The Pirpur Report (1938) was by Raja Syed Mohammad Mehdi of Pirpur; Sharif wrote the 1939 Bihar report.

new.s: 'Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule' (December 1939) was written by:
new.x: Fazlul Huq wrote it in December 1939, after the Pirpur (1938) and Sharif (1939) reports.

new.s: The city where Direct Action Day (1946) led to large-scale killings was:
new.x: Direct Action Day saw the Calcutta killings.

new.s: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded in 1915 at:
new.x: It was founded at Haridwar during the Kumbh Mela in 1915; the RSS was founded at Nagpur.

new.s: Who founded the Hindu Mahasabha?
new.x: Madan Mohan Malaviya founded it; it was first called Sarvadeshik Hindu Sabha and renamed in 1921.

new.s: The RSS was founded by Hedgewar in 1925 at:
new.x: The RSS was founded on 27 September 1925 at Nagpur.

new.s: The quotation on Muslims as the 'greatest bulwark of British power' comes from which book?
o: Pakistan or the Partition of India
new.x: W.W. Hunter wrote it in The Indian Musalmans (1871).
